title: [de] Building static multilingual publishing
excerpt: [de] How pre-rendering six distinct languages with zero runtime client fetching maximizes search crawling and fidelity.
author: Tariq Mahmood
imageAlt: [de] Abstract paint stroke and typographic geometric composition

body.text: [de] Client-rendered single page applications broke the fundamental premise of the web: that every URL corresponds to a tangible HTML document containing real words. When translation layers are added client-side via runtime JSON fetches, international readers and search bots suffer flash of untranslated content and incomplete indexing.

[de] Questo inverts this model. Every article is written as a localized JSON file in Git. At build time, static site generation compiles distinct HTML pages for English, Spanish, French, German, Arabic, and Urdu.
[de] If a page cannot be read with JavaScript disabled, it is not truly published on the open web.

items: [de] Zero runtime database dependencies or API network roundtrips
[de] Deterministic Open Graph and JSON-LD schemas baked into raw HTML markup
[de] Explicit bidirectional rendering with dir=rtl for Arabic and Urdu scripts

body.text: [de] The result is instantaneous first contentful paint, perfect crawlability, and edge deployment that costs nothing to operate at scale.
